scenes.headline: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
scenes.lead: Haloalkanes are alkanes in which one or more hydrogens are replaced by halogen atoms.
groups: Halogen may be F, Cl, Br, or I.
The C-X bond is attached to an alkyl group.
A hydrogen of the benzene nucleus is replaced by a halogen.

figure.caption: Classification of haloalkanes and haloarenes by bond type and halogen count

scenes.headline: Naming the compounds
scenes.lead: Two systems are in common use; the IUPAC name is built from the parent alkane.
groups: Common system: *alkyl halide* — e.g. isopropyl chloride.
IUPAC: *halo* prefix on the alkane — e.g. 2-chloropropane.
Number the chain to give the halogen the lowest locant.
